title: Cato SDP Client Connection Monitoring (Cato Networks)

dataSources: Cato SDP / ZTNA / client session events; `sourcetype=cato:events` or `cato:sase`
app: Cato Networks Events App (Splunkbase 8037); Cato Events API (client / ZTNA-related event families)
spl:
index=sase sourcetype IN ("cato:events","cato:sase") earliest=-24h
| eval u=lower(coalesce(user_name, username, user, email, ""))
| eval auth_ok=if(match(lower(coalesce(auth_result, auth_status, "")),"(?i)success|allow|ok"),1,0)
| eval reason=coalesce(failure_reason, disconnect_reason, error_message, deny_reason, "n/a")
| where match(lower(coalesce(event_sub_type, client_event, "")),"(?i)sdp|ztna|client|vpn|session")
| stats count sum(auth_ok) as successes values(reason) as reasons by u device_os app_version
| eval failures=count-successes
| sort -failures
description: The Cato SDP client delivers ZTNA access for remote users. Connection, authentication, posture, and disconnect-reason events show who cannot reach applications and why — distinguishing client bugs, credential issues, MFA failures, and policy blocks without guessing from help-desk anecdotes.
value: The Cato SDP client delivers ZTNA access for remote users. Timely UC-17.3.30 alerting on 'Cato SDP Client Connection Monitoring (Cato Networks)' reduces unauthorized access, segmentation drift, and NAC policy failures before manual triage or audit channels escalate.
implementation: Normalize `app_version` and alert when a specific version shows elevated failures (upgrade campaign). Build a lookup for “known bad” posture outcomes. Feed top `failure_reason` strings back to IT for knowledge-base articles. Respect privacy: restrict user fields to security roles.

detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Cato Networks SDP (Software-Defined Perimeter) client events in `index=cato` with `sourcetype=cato:events` where `event_type=connectivity` and event relates to SDP/remote user connections. Key fields: `user_name`, `client_version`, `os`, `src_ip`, `pop_name`, `connection_state` (connected/disconnected), `auth_method`, `device_posture`.
• Cato SDP Client provides ZTNA access for remote users. Unlike site tunnels (17.3.29), SDP clients are per-user and connect from anywhere. Connection monitoring ensures remote workers maintain continuous secure access.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Verify SDP client events:
```spl
index=cato sourcetype="cato:events" event_type=connectivity earliest=-24h
| where isnotnull(user_name) AND isnotnull(client_version)
| stats count by connection_state
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Primary search — SDP client health:
```spl
index=cato sourcetype="cato:events" event_type=connectivity earliest=-24h
| where isnotnull(user_name)
| stats latest(connection_state) as current_state latest(client_version) as version latest(os) as os latest(pop_name) as connected_pop by user_name
| eval version_current=if(version>="5.0", "Current", "Outdated")
| stats count by current_state, version_current
```

Understanding this SPL: Shows how many SDP users are currently connected vs disconnected, and how many have current vs outdated client versions. Outdated clients may have unpatched vulnerabilities or lack newer security features. Users disconnected during business hours may have manually disabled the client, bypassing SASE security.

Connection failure analysis:
```spl
index=cato sourcetype="cato:events" event_type=connectivity connection_state=disconnected earliest=-24h
| where isnotnull(user_name)
| stats count by user_name, os, client_version
| where count > 5
| sort - count
```

Step 3 — Validate
(a) In Cato Management: Monitoring > Connected SDP Users.
(b) Connect the SDP client and verify the event.

Step 4 — Operationalize
Dashboard: Row 1 — Connected vs disconnected users. Row 2 — Client version distribution. Row 3 — Frequent disconnections.
Alert: When connected users drop below 80% of active remote workforce during business hours.

Runbook:
1. **Mass disconnection** — Cato PoP issue or DNS resolution failure. Check Cato status page.
2. **Outdated clients** — Push update via MDM. Enforce minimum version in Cato policy.
3. **Individual frequent drops** — User's ISP may be unstable. Or SDP client conflict with local VPN.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting
• **No SDP user events** — SDP client may not be deployed. Check Cato Client Rollout.
• **`client_version` empty** — Older SDP clients may not report version in events.

Step 1 — Configure data collection

Install and configure the add-on referenced in the app field (Cato Networks Events App (Splunkbase 8037); Cato Events API (client / ZTNA-related event families)). Enable the modular input or HEC token that writes sourcetype=cato:events, cato:sase into sase. Default poll interval 300–900 seconds unless the vendor API rate-limits lower. Grant the ingestion role `list_inputs` and `search` on the target index.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Schedule the SPL with earliest=-24h@h and throttle per entity to avoid duplicate pages. Document tunable macros in the comment header. Understanding this SPL: filters in the first pipeline reduce license cost; stats/timechart aggregates define the alert grain; joins/lookups enrich owner or asset metadata for routing.

Step 3 — Validate

Compare `| tstats count where index=... sourcetype=...` against the vendor admin UI inventory count (+/-5%). Spot-check two known entities for field presence (`app_version, auth_ok, device_os, u`). Run `timechart count span=1h` over 7 days to find ingestion gaps longer than two poll intervals.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Add a dashboard row with single-value KPI tiles, a 24-hour timechart, and a drilldown table mirroring the SPL output columns. Route critical severity to the platform on-call channel; route warning to the service owner from the lookup.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

No events: verify forwarder connectivity, HEC token ACLs, and that the modular input appears in `index=_internal source=*splunkd*`. NULL fields: check props/transforms order and TA version. Fewer results than expected: confirm index allow-lists on the search head role and that `_time` uses the correct timezone. API errors: inspect splunkd.log for HTTP 401/429 from the vendor endpoint configured in inputs.conf.
grandmaExplanation: Remote workers use a special app to connect through our security cloud. We monitor whether each person's app is connected and up to date, because if someone disconnects or has an old version, they might be working without our security protection.
hardware: Cato SDP Client on laptops and mobile devices; enforcement still occurs through Cato cloud policy — correlate with Cato Socket sites for hybrid users when applicable.
